headline: Highest risk is medium: Plane can ingest files and use broad egress, but RisingWave has no documented write or egress surface, so pairwise harm is limited and mostly indirect.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can ingest file uploads and hyperlinks, so malicious content could reach its workflow if manually bridged. RisingWave has no documented input surface or parser that would consume Plane output by default, so the interaction is not a default injection channel. The pathway exists only through unusual operator bridging.
conditions: IF an operator copies Plane-generated content into RisingWave-facing configuration or prompts
IF a shared file or message channel is introduced between the two systems
mitigations: Disable copy-paste bridges between systems during review
Use separate workspaces for Plane and RisingWave
Require manual approval before importing Plane exports into RisingWave workflows
Add a provenance label to any transferred text
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance checks at the integration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, notes, issues, and hyperlinks and has broad network egress, so it can expose data if operators move sensitive content into it. RisingWave has no documented data classes touched and no egress, so there is no clear pairwise leakage path from B back out. The main risk is limited to operator-mediated transfer, not default cross-agent exposure.
conditions: IF sensitive files are uploaded into Plane and then exported into RisingWave inputs
IF both systems are pointed at the same shared workspace or export directory
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of Plane uploads
Store RisingWave inputs in a separate directory
Review exports before importing them into the other system
Restrict Plane network destinations where possible
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane cannot write the filesystem and RisingWave has no documented write or mutable-resource scope, so there is no overlapping write surface to conflict over. Broad egress on Plane does not create a write collision with a read-only or unspecified RisingWave profile. The pairwise conflict pathway is therefore not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF RisingWave is later granted filesystem or database write access to the same target as Plane
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state not present in the profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents off the same writable directory
Avoid granting RisingWave write scopes unless needed
Document any shared mutable resource before deployment
Use separate service accounts
requires-engineering: add locking for any future shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can produce issues, tasks, and roadmaps, but RisingWave has no documented action-taking authority or input parser that would automatically trust Plane output. Without a downstream automation surface, Plane's output is not shown to cascade into irreversible actions. The interaction is therefore limited to manual misuse or future integration.
conditions: IF RisingWave is configured to execute actions based on Plane-exported text
IF Plane output is treated as authoritative without human review
mitigations: Require human review of Plane outputs before reuse
Do not wire Plane exports directly into automation
Add validation checks on imported task data
Keep action-taking systems separate from planning systems
requires-engineering: implement schema validation and approval gates

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent in the profiles. Plane is open-source with self-hosted deployment available, and RisingWave has no compliance metadata here, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced. The other agent is not cited separately because no cross-border or policy mismatch is shown.
conditions: IF either deployment is configured to store regulated data in a jurisdiction or service not documented here
IF a future policy or DPA introduces a residency mismatch
mitigations: Confirm data residency before deployment
Avoid placing regulated data into undocumented services
Record retention settings for both systems
Review vendor compliance docs before integration
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets
